title: The normal distribution

points.text: Shape and properties of the normal curve
Normal probabilities and inverse normal by GDC

bigPicture: Many measurements (heights, masses, errors) follow a bell-shaped normal curve. With the mean and standard deviation, the GDC gives any probability or cut-off value.

keyIdeas.answer: Bell-shaped and symmetric about the mean μ (mean = median = mode); spread set by σ; total area 1. About 68% of values lie within 1σ of the mean, 95% within 2σ and 99.7% within 3σ.
A quick sketch with μ marked and the region shaded shows whether the answer should be above or below 0.5 and which tail you need.

keyIdeas.cue: Probabilities and inverse normal on the GDC?
keyIdeas.answer: normalcdf(lower, upper, μ, σ) gives a probability; for a one-sided region use a very large or very small bound. invNorm(area to the left, μ, σ) gives the value x with that probability below it.

keyTerms.def: continuous, symmetric, bell-shaped distribution X ~ N(μ, σ²)
finding x from a given probability

misconceptions.wrong: N(μ, σ²): the second number is σ
misconceptions.right: It is the variance; enter σ (its square root) on the GDC.
invNorm uses the area to the LEFT; convert first.

practice.prompt: X ~ N(50, 4²). Write down P(X > 50). Given P(X < 46) = 0.159, find P(46 < X < 54).
Masses of packets are N(250, 6²) grams. (a) Find P(mass < 240 g). (b) Find the mass exceeded by 10% of packets.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

memorise: GDC normalcdf and invNorm, including which area invNorm uses
